steps.observation: Work on this for 900 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three of the principal factors that set the stage for World War I:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • Major European powers dramatically expanded and modernized their armies and navies in the decades before 1914, creating a climate in which many leaders believed that war was both inevitable and, in some circles, desirable.  
   • Germany’s naval buildup to challenge British sea power, along with large standing armies on the continent, fostered mutual suspicion and made rapid mobilization plans (such as Germany’s Schlieffen Plan and France’s Plan XVII) central to national strategy.

2. Entangling alliances  
   • Two dominant alliance blocs solidified: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   • These alliances were intended as deterrents but ultimately ensured that any localized conflict—such as that between Austria-Hungary and Serbia after the assassination in Sarajevo—would quickly draw in multiple great powers.

3. Nationalism and imperial rivalries  
   • Intense nationalist sentiment stoked ambitions for territorial expansion or defense of ethnic kin (e.g., Pan-Slavism among Serbs backed by Russia; German and French claims over Alsace-Lorraine).  
   • Imperial competition for colonies and global influence heightened distrust—especially between Britain and Germany in Africa and Asia—and fed domestic calls for assertive foreign policies.

(Additional sparks, such as the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and the subsequent July Crisis, transformed these underlying causes into open conflict.)
